text: INTRODUCTION It was a sense of continuity which inspired the saying, “The king is dead; long live the king.” A similar sense would justify the statement, “The Council is over; the Council has just begun.” The Council is indeed over.
text_raw:
INTRODUCTION 
It was a sense of continuity which inspired the saying, “The king 
is dead; long live the king.” A similar sense would justify the 
statement, “The Council is over; the Council has just begun.” 
The Council is indeed over.

text: John XXIII had been Pope for merely ninety days when, on January 25, 1959, he made the first and completely unexpected announcement of his plan to con¬ voke the Church’s Twenty-First Ecumenical Council, the first since Vatican I of 1869-70.

John XXIII had been Pope for 
merely ninety days when, on January 25, 1959, he made the first 
and completely unexpected announcement of his plan to con¬ 
voke the Church’s Twenty-First Ecumenical Council, the first 
since Vatican I of 1869-70.

text: On October 11, 1962, after nearly four years of exhaustive preparation, the Council finally opened.

text: In a positive and optimistic speech, the eighty-year-old Pope John gently chided the prophets of doom within the Church and spoke of the world’s need for the medicine of mercy.

text: However, since God speaks in sacred Scripture through men in human fashion,33 the interpreter of sacred Scripture, in order to see clearly what God wanted to communicate to us, should carefully investigate what meaning the sacred writ¬ ers really intended, and what God wanted to manifest by means of their words.34 Those who search out the intention of the sacred writers must, among other things, have regard for “literary forms.” For truth is proposed and expressed in a variety of ways, de¬ pending on whether a text is history of one kind or another, or whether its form is that of prophecy, poetry, or some other type of speech.

However, since God speaks in sacred Scripture through 
men in human fashion,33 the interpreter of sacred Scripture, 
in order to see clearly what God wanted to communicate to 
us, should carefully investigate what meaning the sacred writ¬

means of their words.34 
Those who search out the intention of the sacred writers 
must, among other things, have regard for “literary forms.”

text: The interpreter must investigate what meaning the sacred writer intended to express and actually expressed in particular circumstances as he used contemporary literary forms in accordance with the situation of his own time and culture.36 For the correct understanding of what the sacred author wanted to assert, due attention must be paid to the customary and characteristic styles of perceiving, speaking, and narrating which prevailed at the time of the sacred writer, and to the customs men normally followed at that period in their everyday dealings with one another.36 But, since holy Scripture must be read and interpreted ac¬ cording to the same Spirit by whom it was written,37 no less serious attention must be given to the content and unity of the whole of Scripture, if the meaning of the sacred texts is to be correctly brought to light.

text: It is the goal of this most sacred Council to intensify the daily growth of Catholics in Christian living; to make more responsive to the requirements of our times those Church ob¬ servances which are open to adaptation; to nurture whatever can contribute to the unity of all who believe in Christ; and to strengthen those aspects of the Church which can help summon all of mankind into her embrace.

daily growth of Catholics in Christian living; to make more 
responsive to the requirements of our times those Church ob¬ 
servances which are open to adaptation; to nurture whatever 
can contribute to the unity of all who believe in Christ; and 
to strengthen those aspects of the Church which can help 
summon all of mankind into her embrace.

text: Whatever the regrettable misunderstandings that turned the “rights of man” into a rallying cry of the Church’s bitter foes in the 18th and 19th centuries and entrenched the Church in a role of intransigent resistance to movements for social revolution in many parts of the world, the Council now makes it unequivo¬ cally plain that the Church intends to play its true historic role as a champion of human rights and to align itself with those who fight for these rights.
text_raw:
Whatever the regrettable misunderstandings that turned the “rights of man” 
into a rallying cry of the Church’s bitter foes in the 18th and 19th centuries and 
entrenched the Church in a role of intransigent resistance to movements for 
social revolution in many parts of the world, the Council now makes it unequivo¬ 
cally plain that the Church intends to play its true historic role as a champion of 
human rights and to align itself with those who fight for these rights.

text: 242 THE DOCUMENTS OF VATICAN II toward unity, a process of wholesome socialization and of association in civic and economic realms.
text_raw:
242 THE DOCUMENTS OF VATICAN II 
toward unity, a process of wholesome socialization and of 
association in civic and economic realms.

text: For the promotion of unity belongs to the innermost nature of the Church, since she is, “by her relationship with Christ, both a sacramental sign and an instrument of intimate union with God, and of the unity of all mankind.”133 Thus she shows the world that an authentic union, social and external, results from a union of minds and hearts, name¬ ly, from that faith and charity by which her own unity is unbreakably rooted in the Holy Spirit.
text_raw:
For the promotion 
of unity belongs to the innermost nature of the Church, since 
she is, “by her relationship with Christ, both a sacramental 
sign and an instrument of intimate union with God, and of 
the unity of all mankind.”133 
Thus she shows the world that an authentic union, social 
and external, results from a union of minds and hearts, name¬ 
ly, from that faith and charity by which her own unity is 
unbreakably rooted in the Holy Spirit.

text: For the force which the Church can inject into the modern society of man con¬ sists in that faith and charity put into vital practice, not in any external dominion exercised by merely human means.

the Church can inject into the modern society of man con¬

text: Hence the Church by her very universality can be a very close bond between diverse human communities and nations, provided these trust her and truly acknowledge her right to true freedom in fulfilling her mis¬ sion.

text: For this reason, the Church admonishes her own sons, but also humanity as a whole, to overcome all strife between nations and races in this family spirit of God’s children, and in the same way, to give internal strength to human associa¬ tions which are just.

text: Above all let them take to heart the words which this Council has spoken: “Because the human race today is joining more and more in civic, economic, and social unity, it is that much more necessary that priests, united in concern and effort under the leadership of the bish¬ ops and the Supreme Pontiff, wipe out every ground of division, so that the whole human race may be brought into the unity of the family of God.”142 Although by the power of the Holy Spirit the Church has remained the faithful spouse of her Lord and has never ceased to be the sign of salvation on earth, still she is very well aware that among her members,143 both clerical and lay, some have been unfaithful to the Spirit of God during the course of many centuries.

text: The faithful are bound on Sundays and feast days to at¬ tend the divine liturgy or, according to the regulations or custom of their own rite, the celebration of the Divine praises.31 That the faithful may be able to satisfy their ob¬ ligation more easily, it is decreed that this obligation can be fulfilled from the Vespers of the vigil to the end of the Sun¬ day or the feast day.32 The faithful are earnestly exhorted to receive holy Communion on these days, and indeed more frequently—even daily.33 16.

text: The Eastern Churches in communion with the Apostolic See of Rome have a special role to play in promoting the unity of all Christians, particularly Easterners, according to the principles of this sacred Synod's Decree on Ecumenism: first of all by prayer, then by the example of their lives, by religious fidelity to ancient Eastern traditions,48 by greater mutual knowledge, by collaboration, and by a brotherly re¬ gard for objects40 and attitudes.50 25.

mutual knowledge, by collaboration, and by a brotherly re¬ 
gard for objects40 and attitudes.50

text: In view of the principles recalled above, Eastern Chris¬ tians who are separated in good faith from the Catholic Church, if they ask of their own accord and have the right dispositions, may be granted the sacraments of penance, the Eucharist, and the anointing of the sick.

text: RELIGIOUS LIFE INTRODUCTION The aim of Vatican Council II is stated in the words of Pope John XXIII: to invoke a new Pentecost, calling for renewal of the Church in her head and in all her members, for her reformation in the reflection of Christ in the Gospels.

RELIGIOUS LIFE 
INTRODUCTION 
The aim of Vatican Council II is stated in the words of 
Pope John XXIII: to invoke a new Pentecost, calling for 
renewal of the Church in her head and in all her members, 
for her reformation in the reflection of Christ in the Gospels.

text: REASONS FOR RENEWAL To anyone who knows the history of the Church it is ob¬ vious that the Holy Spirit has at all times raised in the Church men and women who, under His guidance and in cor¬ respondence to the needs of the Church, have initiated spir¬ itual movements which were then continued and expanded by the religious families they founded.

REASONS FOR RENEWAL

Church men and women who, under His guidance and in cor¬ 
respondence to the needs of the Church, have initiated spir¬ 
itual movements which were then continued and expanded 
by the religious families they founded.

text: But it is not less clear that the same Spirit who continues to evoke new spiritual movements in the People of God is also constantly urging those religious who already have dedicated their lives to a certain type of service in the Church, to reflect seriously and actively so as to discover how their institute could and should be adapted ever more perfectly to the continuously chang¬ ing circumstances of their own times.

text: Some types of the apostolate demand very special forma¬ tion. a) When the apostolate is one of making the gospel known and men holy, the laity must be specially formed to engage in conversation with others, believers or non-believers, in order to manifest Christ’s message to all men.75 Since in our times, variations of materialism are rampant everywhere, even among Catholics, the laity should not only learn doctrine more carefully, especially those main points which are the subjects of controversy, but should also provide the witness of an evangelical life in contrast to all forms of materialism. b) With respect to the Christian renewal of the temporal or¬ der, laymen should be instructed in the true meaning and value of temporal things, both in themselves and in their rela¬ tion to the total fulfillment of the human person.

MISSIONS 
It is worth noting that the Decree on the Missionary 
Activity of the Church (Ad Gentes) and the basic decree of 
Vatican II, the Constitution on the Church (Lumen Gen¬ 
tium), both begin with a reference to the same passage from 
Isaiah which presents the People of God as being sent into 
the world to be the light and salvation of the unbelieving 
nations—the gentes.

text: The connection between these two docu¬ ments, however, goes much deeper than the similarity of the initial words; there is a substantial connection between the two.

initial words; there is a substantial connection between the 
two.

Both documents illustrate the rediscovery of the true bibli¬ 
cal nature of the Church and its mission to unbelievers.

text: The mission of the Church to “those without,” as belonging to the essential nature of the People of God, receives major stress in the Constitution on the Church; the Church has been sent to unbelievers to be the “sacrament of unity of the whole human race.” The decree on the missions continues this theme, not merely by way of repeating it, but by locating this mission within the history and geography of the globe and in specifying its yet unaccomplished task in the context of the modern world.

text: Part of its duty is to promote the education of the young in several ways: namely, by overseeing the duties and rights of parents and of others who have a role in education, and by providing them with assistance; by implementing the principle of subsidiarity* and completing the task of education, with attention to parental wishes, whenever the efforts of parents and of other groups are insufficient; and, moreover, by build¬ ing its own schools and institutes, as the common good may demand.18 Finally, the office of educating belongs by a unique title to the Church, not merely because she deserves recognition as a human society capable of educating, but most of all because she has the responsibility of announcing the way of salvation to all men, of communicating the life of Christ to those who believe, and of assisting them with ceaseless concern so that they may grow into the fullness of that same life.19 As a mother, the Church is bound to give these children of hers the kind of education through which their entire lives can be penetrated with the spirit of Christ, while at the same time she offers her services to all peoples by way of promoting the full development of the human person, for the welfare of earthly society and the building of a world fashioned more humanly.20 4.

text: €50 THE DOCUMENTS OF VATICAN II confides the most serious task of preparing her own students not only for the priestly ministry, but especially for teaching in seats of higher Church studies, for advancing branches of knowledge by their own efforts, and for undertaking the more arduous challenges of the intellectual apostolate.49 It is also the responsibility of these faculties to explore more profoundly the various areas of the sacred disciplines so that day by day a deeper understanding of sacred revelation will be developed, the treasure of Christian wisdom handed down by our ancestors will be more plainly brought to view, dia¬ logue will be fostered with our separated brothers and with non-Christians, and solutions will be found for problems raised by the development of doctrine.50 Therefore, these ecclesiastical faculties should zealously pro¬ mote the sacred and related sciences by an opportune revision of their own bylaws.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Also, the responsibility of that society to provide education for all children as a matter of justice is given the emphasis that it deserves.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The characteristic Roman Catholic emphasis on the rights and responsibility of parents for the education of their chil¬ dren is present throughout the document, and I welcome this as a check on the tendency of many Protestants to assume that the state or the community acting through agencies of the state is the educator.

and responsibility of parents for the education of their chil¬

as a check on the tendency of many Protestants to assume 
that the state or the community acting through agencies of 
the state is the educator.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: I think that there is a danger in this country of being too uncritical of the idea of a monopoly of the state in education.
text_raw:

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Here I am led to sug¬ gest that probably this will never be given adequate emphasis unless Christians feel that they have a stake in public educa¬ tion in the case of their own children.

text: Even though the fact and claims of a pluralistic society are recognized, and even though the Council’s splen¬ did statement on religious liberty is seen to have significance for the life of the Christian school, I doubt if a wholly sep¬ arate Christian education, in most cases under the leadership of the clergy, can really initiate children into the life of a very mixed society or expose them adequately to the subject matter of secular disciplines.

text: Also, given the fact of the millions of Catholic children in parochial schools, the nation has a stake in the quality of their educa¬ tion, and it should not express its interest here by demanding standards in a way that would drive the parochial schools out of existence.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The issues are many—the dignity of the Christian, the foundations of Christian free¬ dom, its object or content, its limits and their criterion, the measure of its responsible use, its relation to the legitimate reaches of authority and to the saving counsels of prudence, the perils that lurk in it, and the forms of corruption to which it is prone.
text_raw:
The issues are many—the 
dignity of the Christian, the foundations of Christian free¬ 
dom, its object or content, its limits and their criterion, the 
measure of its responsible use, its relation to the legitimate 
reaches of authority and to the saving counsels of prudence, 
the perils that lurk in it, and the forms of corruption 
to which it is prone.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: All these issues must be considered in a spirit of sober and informed reflection.
text_raw:
All these issues must be considered in a 
spirit of sober and informed reflection.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: A sense of the dignity of the human person has been im¬ pressing itself more and more deeply on the consciousness of contemporary man.1 And the demand is increasingly made that men should act on their own judgment, enjoying and making use of a responsible freedom, not driven by coercion but motivated by a sense of duty.
text_raw:
A sense of the dignity of the human person has been im¬ 
pressing itself more and more deeply on the consciousness of 
contemporary man.1 And the demand is increasingly made 
that men should act on their own judgment, enjoying and 
making use of a responsible freedom, not driven by coercion 
but motivated by a sense of duty.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The demand is also made that constitutional limits should be set to the powers of gov¬ ernment, in order that there may be no encroachment on the rightful freedom of the person and of associations.
text_raw:
The demand is also made 
that constitutional limits should be set to the powers of gov¬ 
ernment, in order that there may be no encroachment on the 
rightful freedom of the person and of associations.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This demand for freedom in human society chiefly regards the quest for the values proper to the human spirit.
text_raw:
This demand for freedom in human society chiefly regards 
the quest for the values proper to the human spirit.

text: First,3 this sacred Synod professes its belief that God him- “signs of the times.” Hence the Declaration begins by noting two facts.
text_raw:
First,3 this sacred Synod professes its belief that God him-

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The first is the recent rise of man’s personal consciousness, his sense of self¬ hood.
text_raw:
The 
first is the recent rise of man’s personal consciousness, his sense of self¬ 
hood.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This increasing awareness of the dignity of the human person marks a progress of civilization.
text_raw:
This increasing awareness of the dignity of the human person marks a 
progress of civilization.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: It is the good which has come out of the great evil of totalitarianism, which brutally refuses to acknowledge the reality of man’s selfhood.
text_raw:
It is the good which has come out of the great evil 
of totalitarianism, which brutally refuses to acknowledge the reality of 
man’s selfhood.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The second fact is the related rise of man’s political con¬ sciousness, his aspiration to live as a free man under a limited government which puts no obstacles to his pursuit of truth and virtue, and, in particular, leaves him unhindered in the free exercise of religion in society.
text_raw:
The second fact is the related rise of man’s political con¬ 
sciousness, his aspiration to live as a free man under a limited government 
which puts no obstacles to his pursuit of truth and virtue, and, in particular, 
leaves him unhindered in the free exercise of religion in society.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: (Happily, the Declaration adopts the classical phrase which the Founding Fathers like¬ wise adopted when framing the First Amendment in 1791.) In thus acknowledging certain realities of contemporary life, the Declaration also establishes direct continuity with two basic doctrinal themes of John XXIII in the encyclical ‘‘Pacem in Terris”: the dignity of the human person and the consequent necessity of constitutional limits to the powers of government.
text_raw:
(Happily, 
the Declaration adopts the classical phrase which the Founding Fathers like¬ 
wise adopted when framing the First Amendment in 1791.) 
In thus acknowledging certain realities of contemporary life, the Declaration 
also establishes direct continuity with two basic doctrinal themes of John 
XXIII in the encyclical ‘‘Pacem in Terris”: the dignity of the human person 
and the consequent necessity of constitutional limits to the powers of 
government.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The language of these opening sentences is, in fact, taken from this great encyclical.
text_raw:

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The issue of religious freedom arises in the political and social order—in the order of the relationship between the people and government and between man and man.
text_raw:
The issue of religious freedom arises in the political and social order—in 
the order of the relationship between the people and government and between 
man and man.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This is the order of human rights, and in it the principle of freedom is paramount.
text_raw:
This is the order of human rights, and in it the principle of 
freedom is paramount.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: However, man’s life is also lived in another order of reality—in the spiritual order of man’s relationship to what is objectively true and morally good.
text_raw:
However, man’s life is also lived in another order of 
reality—in the spiritual order of man’s relationship to what is objectively 
true and morally good.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This is the order of duty and obligation.
text_raw: This is the order of duty and obligation.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: In it a man acts freely indeed, but under moral imperatives, which bind in con¬ science.
text_raw:
In it a 
man acts freely indeed, but under moral imperatives, which bind in con¬ 
science.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: No man may plead “rights” in the face of the truth or claim “freedom” from the moral law.
text_raw:
No man may plead “rights” in the face of the truth or claim 
“freedom” from the moral law.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The distinction between these two orders of reality would be admitted by all men of good sense.
text_raw:
The distinction between these two orders 
of reality would be admitted by all men of good sense.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The underlying in¬ tention of these two paragraphs of the Declaration is to make this distinction clear, lest religious freedom be made a pretext for moral anarchy.
text_raw:
The underlying in¬ 
tention of these two paragraphs of the Declaration is to make this distinction 
clear, lest religious freedom be made a pretext for moral anarchy.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: However, the distinction is stated in Catholic terms.
text_raw: However, the distinction is stated in Catholic terms.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: For the Catholic, the “truth” is not a vague abstraction; it subsists in the Church, is taught by the Church, is believed by the Church.
text_raw:
For the Catholic, the 
“truth” is not a vague abstraction; it subsists in the Church, is taught by 
the Church, is believed by the Church.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Moreover, this truth about God and about His will for men is not the private possession of a party or sect; it is to be taught to all men, and all nations are to be its disciples.
text_raw:
Moreover, this truth about God and 
about His will for men is not the private possession of a party or sect; it 
is to be taught to all men, and all nations are to be its disciples.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: It is not to be thrust by force upon any man; in the order of man’s relationship to truth, coercion has no place whatsoever.
text_raw:
It is not 
to be thrust by force upon any man; in the order of man’s relationship to 
truth, coercion has no place whatsoever.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Consequently, as the Declaration will later make clear, religious freedom is an exigence of religious truth as conceived by the Church.
text_raw:
Consequently, as the Declaration 
will later make clear, religious freedom is an exigence of religious truth as 
conceived by the Church.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: On the other hand, no man may say of the religious truth which subsists in the Church: “It is no concern of mine.” Once given by Christ to His true Church, the true religion remains the one way in which all men are bound to serve God and save themselves.
text_raw:
On the other hand, no man may say of the religious truth which subsists in 
the Church: “It is no concern of mine.” Once given by Christ to His true 
Church, the true religion remains the one way in which all men are bound to 
serve God and save themselves.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Consequently, religious freedom is not a title to exemption from the obligation to “observe all things whatsoever I have enjoined upon you.” In fine, a harmony exists between man’s duty of free obedience to the truth and his right to the free exercise of religion in society.
text_raw:
Consequently, religious freedom is not a title 
to exemption from the obligation to “observe all things whatsoever I have 
enjoined upon you.” In fine, a harmony exists between man’s duty of free 
obedience to the truth and his right to the free exercise of religion in 
society.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The duty does not diminish the right, nor does the right diminish the duty.
text_raw:
The duty does not diminish the right, nor does the right diminish 
the duty.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,

Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: On their part, all men are bound to seek the truth, especially in what concerns God and His Church, and to embrace the truth they come to know, and to hold fast to it.
text_raw:
On their part, all men are bound to seek the truth, especially 
in what concerns God and His Church, and to embrace the

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This sacred Synod likewise professes its belief that it is upon the human conscience that these obligations fall and exert their binding force.
text_raw:
This sacred Synod likewise professes its belief that it is 
upon the human conscience that these obligations fall and 
exert their binding force.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The truth cannot impose itself ex¬ cept by virtue of its own truth, as it makes its entrance into the mind at once quietly and with power.
text_raw:
The truth cannot impose itself ex¬ 
cept by virtue of its own truth, as it makes its entrance into 
the mind at once quietly and with power.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Religious freedom, in turn, which men demand as necessary to fulfill their duty to worship God, has to do with immunity from coercion in civil society.
text_raw:
Religious freedom, 
in turn, which men demand as necessary to fulfill their duty 
to worship God, has to do with immunity from coercion in 
civil society.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Therefore, it leaves untouched traditional Cath¬ olic doctrine on the moral duty of men and societies toward the true religion and toward the one Church of Christ.
text_raw:
Therefore, it leaves untouched traditional Cath¬ 
olic doctrine on the moral duty of men and societies toward

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Over and above all this, in taking up the matter of religious freedom this sacred Synod intends to develop the doctrine of recent Popes on the inviolable rights of the human person and on the constitutional order of society.4 freedom.
text_raw:
Over and above all this, in taking up the matter of religious 
freedom this sacred Synod intends to develop the doctrine 
of recent Popes on the inviolable rights of the human person

freedom.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Neither the spirit of ecumenism nor the principle of religious freedom requires that the Church refrain from stating publicly what she believes herself to be.
text_raw:
Neither the spirit of ecumenism nor the principle of religious 
freedom requires that the Church refrain from stating publicly what she 
believes herself to be.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The demands of truth are no more opposed to the demands of freedom than they are opposed to the demands of love.
text_raw:
The demands of truth are no more opposed to the 
demands of freedom than they are opposed to the demands of love.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: In no other conciliar document is it so explicitly stated that the intention of the Council is to “develop” Catholic doctrine.
text_raw:
In no other conciliar document is it so explicitly stated that the intention 
of the Council is to “develop” Catholic doctrine.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This is significant, since it is an avowal that the tradition of the Church is a tradition of progress in understanding the truth.
text_raw:
This is significant, since 
it is an avowal that the tradition of the Church is a tradition of progress

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: The basic truth here is the concept of the “citizen” as stated by Pius XII—the man who “feels within himself a consciousness of his own personality, of his duties, and of his rights, joined with a respect for the freedom of others” (Christmas Discourse, 1945).
text_raw:
The basic truth here is the concept of the 
“citizen” as stated by Pius XII—the man who “feels within himself a 
consciousness of his own personality, of his duties, and of his rights, joined 
with a respect for the freedom of others” (Christmas Discourse, 1945).

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: This conception, as ,the Declaration will say, is deeply rooted both in the Christian tradition and in the tradition of reason.
text_raw:
This 
conception, as ,the Declaration will say, is deeply rooted both in the Christian 
tradition and in the tradition of reason.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: In recent times, it was Leo XIII (in “Rerum Novarum”) who first began to move it, as it were, to the forefront of Catholic social teaching.
text_raw:
In recent times, it was Leo XIII 
(in “Rerum Novarum”) who first began to move it, as it were, to the forefront 
of Catholic social teaching.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Pius XII continued this development, drawing out the implications of the dignity of man in terms of his duties and rights.
text_raw:
Pius XII continued this development, drawing 
out the implications of the dignity of man in terms of his duties and rights.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: He also brought forward the correlative truth, that the primary function of government is to acknowledge, protect, vindicate, and facilitate the exercise of the rights of man.
text_raw:
He also brought forward the correlative truth, that the primary function 
of government is to acknowledge, protect, vindicate, and facilitate the 
exercise of the rights of man.

chapter_title: Part 111, Aug. 6, 1964; AAS 56 (1964), pp. 637-659; Second Vatican Council,
text: Both of these truths were taken up by John XXIII, chiefly in “Pacem in Terris,” in which they are given an almost systematic form of statement.
text_raw:
Both of these truths were taken up by John 
XXIII, chiefly in “Pacem in Terris,” in which they are given an almost

text_raw:

OF RELIGIOUS FREEDOM 
2.

text: This Vatican Synod declares that the human person has a right to religious freedom.5 This freedom means that all men are the questions to which, for the first time, the Church gives an unmis¬ takably clear and entirely unambiguous answer.
text_raw:
This Vatican Synod declares that the human person has a 
right to religious freedom.5 This freedom means that all men 
are the questions to which, for the first time, the Church gives an unmis¬ 
takably clear and entirely unambiguous answer.

text: The Council brings forth out of the treasury of truth a doctrine that is at once new and also in harmony with traditional teaching.
text_raw:
The Council brings forth 
out of the treasury of truth a doctrine that is at once new and also in 
harmony with traditional teaching.

text: The doctrinal substance of the Declaration is stated in this paragraph, which defines what religious freedom is and affirms its status as a human— and therefore civil—right.
text_raw:
The doctrinal substance of the Declaration is stated in this paragraph, 
which defines what religious freedom is and affirms its status as a human— 
and therefore civil—right.

text: A right is a moral claim made on others that they either give me something or do something for me or refrain from doing something.
text_raw:
A right is a moral claim made on others that 
they either give me something or do something for me or refrain from doing 
something.

text: Two questions always arise.
text_raw: Two questions always arise.

text: First, what is the moral claim I make on others, or in other words, what is the object or content of my right?
text_raw:
First, what is the moral claim I make 
on others, or in other words, what is the object or content of my right?

text: Second, on what grounds do I make this moral claim, or in other words, what is the foundation of my right?
text_raw:
Second, on what grounds do I make this moral claim, or in other words, 
what is the foundation of my right?

text: The Declaration first defines religious freedom in terms of its object or content.
text_raw:
The Declaration first defines religious freedom in terms of its object or 
content.

text: The moral claim that every man makes on others—on individuals, groups, political or social powers—is that they refrain from bringing coercion to bear on him in all matters religious.
text_raw:
The moral claim that every man makes on others—on individuals, 
groups, political or social powers—is that they refrain from bringing coercion 
to bear on him in all matters religious.

text: This claim is twofold.
text_raw: This claim is twofold.

text: First, no man is to be forced to act in a manner contrary to his personal beliefs; second, no man is to be forcibly restrained from acting in accordance with his beliefs.
text_raw:
First, no man 
is to be forced to act in a manner contrary to his personal beliefs; second, 
no man is to be forcibly restrained from acting in accordance with his 
beliefs.

text: The affirmation of this latter immunity is the new thing, which is in harmony with the older affirmation of the former immunity.
text_raw:

Catholic- Orthodox 
Declaration 
On December 7, 1965, Pope Paul in Rome and Patriarch 
Athenagoras in Istanbul issued this text concerning the 
events of 1054 that led to a breach between the Roman 
Catholic Church and the Orthodox Church of Constantinople.

text: Grateful to God who mercifully favored them with a fra¬ ternal meeting at those holy places where the mystery of salvation was accomplished through the death and resurrec¬ tion of the Lord Jesus, and where the Church was born through the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I have not lost sight of the determination each then felt to omit nothing thereafter which charity might inspire and which could facilitate the develop¬ ment of the fraternal relations thus taken up between the Roman Catholic Church and the Orthodox Church of Con¬ stantinople.

Grateful to God who mercifully favored them with a fra¬ 
ternal meeting at those holy places where the mystery of 
salvation was accomplished through the death and resurrec¬ 
tion of the Lord Jesus, and where the Church was born 
through the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, Pope Paul VI 
and Patriarch Athenagoras I have not lost sight of the 
determination each then felt to omit nothing thereafter which 
charity might inspire and which could facilitate the develop¬ 
ment of the fraternal relations thus taken up between the 
Roman Catholic Church and the Orthodox Church of Con¬ 
stantinople.

text: Closing Messages of the Council On December 8, at the close of the solemn ceremonies mark¬ ing the end of the Second Vatican Council, Pope Paul spoke to the Council Fathers, and cardinals read messages, in the name of the Council Fathers, to various groups of people: rulers, intellectuals and scientists, artists, women, the poor, sick, and suffering, workers, and youth.

Closing Messages 
of the Council 
On December 8, at the close of the solemn ceremonies mark¬

to the Council Fathers, and cardinals read messages, in the 
name of the Council Fathers, to various groups of people: 
rulers, intellectuals and scientists, artists, women, the poor, 
sick, and suffering, workers, and youth.

text: In this universal assembly, in this privileged point of time and space, there converge together the past, the present, and the future—the past: for here, gathered in this spot, we have the Church of Christ with her tradition, her history, her Councils, her doctors, her saints; the present: for we are taking leave of one another to go out toward the world of today with its miseries, its sufferings, its sins, but also with its prodigious accomplish¬ ments, its values, its virtues; and lastly the future is here in the urgent appeal of the peoples of the world for more justice, in their will for peace, in their conscious or unconscious thirst for a higher life, that life precisely which the Church of Christ can and wishes to give them.

text: To Rulers (Read by Achille Cardinal Lienart of Lille, assisted by Ber¬ nard Cardinal Alfrink of Utrecht and Giovanni Cardinal Colombo of Milan.) the message of truth entrusted to the Church and an effort 
at more perfect docility to the spirit of truth?

text: Hence our paths could not fail to cross.
text_raw: Hence our paths could not fail to cross.

text: Your road is ours.
text_raw: Your road is ours.

text: Your paths are never foreign to ours.
text_raw: Your paths are never foreign to ours.

text: We are the friends of your vocation as searchers, companions in your fatigues, admirers of your successes, and, if necessary, consolers in your discouragement and your failures.
text_raw:
We are the friends of 
your vocation as searchers, companions in your fatigues, 
admirers of your successes, and, if necessary, consolers in 
your discouragement and your failures.

text: Hence for you also we have a message, and it is this:
text_raw: Hence for you also we have a message, and it is this:

text: Continue your search without tiring and without ever despair¬ ing of the truth.
text_raw:
Continue your search without tiring and without ever despair¬ 
ing of the truth.

text: Recall the words of one of your great friends, St. Augustine: “Let us seek with the desire to find, and find with the desire to seek still more.” Happy are those who, while possessing the truth, search more earnestly for it in order to renew it, deepen it, and transmit it to others.
text_raw:
Recall the words of one of your great friends, 
St. Augustine: “Let us seek with the desire to find, and find 
with the desire to seek still more.” Happy are those who, while 
possessing the truth, search more earnestly for it in order 
to renew it, deepen it, and transmit it to others.

text: Happy also are those who, not having found it, are working toward it with a sincere heart.
text_raw:
Happy also 
are those who, not having found it, are working toward it 
with a sincere heart.

text: May they seek the light of tomorrow with the light of today until they reach the fullness of light.
text_raw:
May they seek the light of tomorrow 
with the light of today until they reach the fullness of light.

text: But do not forget that if thinking is something great, it is first a duty.
text_raw:
But do not forget that if thinking is something great, it is 
first a duty.

text: Woe to him who voluntarily closes his eyes to the light.
text_raw:
Woe to him who voluntarily closes his eyes to 
the light.

text: Thinking is also a responsibility, so woe to those who darken the spirit by the thousand tricks which degrade it, make it proud, deceive and deform it.
text_raw:
Thinking is also a responsibility, so woe to those 
who darken the spirit by the thousand tricks which degrade it, 
make it proud, deceive and deform it.

text: What other basic principle is there for men of science except to think rightly?
text_raw:
What other basic 
principle is there for men of science except to think rightly?

text: For this purpose, without troubling your efforts, without dazzling brilliance, we come to offer you the light of our mysterious lamp which is faith.
text_raw:
For this purpose, without troubling your efforts, without 
dazzling brilliance, we come to offer you the light of our 
mysterious lamp which is faith.

text: He who entrusted this lamp to us is the sovereign Master of all thought, He whose humble disciples we are, the only one who said and could have said: “I am the light of the world, I am the way, the truth, and the life.” These words have meaning for you.
text_raw:
He who entrusted this lamp to 
us is the sovereign Master of all thought, He whose humble 
disciples we are, the only one who said and could have said: 
“I am the light of the world, I am the way, the truth, and the 
life.” 
These words have meaning for you.

text: Never perhaps, thank God, has there been so clear a possibility as today of a deep understanding between real science and real faith, mutual servants of one another in the one truth.
text_raw:
Never perhaps, thank 
God, has there been so clear a possibility as today of a deep 
understanding between real science and real faith, mutual 
servants of one another in the one truth.

text: Do not stand in the way of this important meeting.
text_raw:
Do not stand in the 
way of this important meeting.

text: Have confidence in faith, this great friend of intelligence.
text_raw:
Have confidence in faith, this 
great friend of intelligence.

text: Enlighten yourselves with its light in order to take hold of truth, the whole truth.
text_raw:
Enlighten yourselves with its 
light in order to take hold of truth, the whole truth.

text: This is the wish, the encouragement, and the hope, which, before disbanding, is expressed to you by the Fathers of the entire world assembled at Rome in Council.
text_raw:
This is 
the wish, the encouragement, and the hope, which, before 
disbanding, is expressed to you by the Fathers of the entire

text: 732 THE DOCUMENTS OF VATICAN II To Artists (Read by Leo Cardinal Suenens of M alines-Brussels [Belgium], assisted by Lawrence Cardinal Shehan of Baltimore and Jaime Cardinal de Barros Camara of Rio de Janeiro.) We now address you, artists, who are taken up with beauty and work for it: poets and literary men, painters, sculptors, architects, musicians, men devoted to the theater and the cinema.
text_raw:
732 THE DOCUMENTS OF VATICAN II 
To Artists 
(Read by Leo Cardinal Suenens of M alines-Brussels [Belgium],

text: To all of you, the Church of the Council declares to you through our voice: if you are friends of genuine art, you are our friends.
text_raw:
To all of you, the Church of the Council declares to 
you through our voice: if you are friends of genuine art,

text: The Church has long since joined in alliance with you.
text_raw: The Church has long since joined in alliance with you.

text: You have built and adorned her temples, celebrated her dogmas, enriched her liturgy.
text_raw:
You 
have built and adorned her temples, celebrated her dogmas, 
enriched her liturgy.

text: You have aided her in translating her divine message in the language of forms and figures, making the invisible world palpable.
text_raw:
You have aided her in translating her 
divine message in the language of forms and figures, making 
the invisible world palpable.

text: Today, as yesterday, the Church needs you and turns to you.
text_raw:
Today, as yesterday, the Church 
needs you and turns to you.

text: She tells you through our voice:
text_raw: She tells you through our voice:

text: Do not allow an alliance as fruitful as this to be broken.
text_raw: Do not allow an alliance as fruitful as this to be broken.

text: Do not refuse to put your talents at the service of divine truth.
text_raw:
Do 
not refuse to put your talents at the service of divine truth.

text: Do not close your mind to the breath of the Holy Spirit.
text_raw: Do not close your mind to the breath of the Holy Spirit.

text: This world in which we live needs beauty in order not to sink into despair.
text_raw:
This world in which we live needs beauty in order not to 
sink into despair.

text: It is beauty, like truth, which brings joy to the heart of man and is that precious fruit which resists the wear and tear of time, which unites generations and makes them share things in admiration.
text_raw:
It is beauty, like truth, which brings joy to 
the heart of man and is that precious fruit which resists the 
wear and tear of time, which unites generations and makes 
them share things in admiration.

text: And all of this is through your hands.
text_raw:
And all of this is through 
your hands.

text: May these hands be pure and disinterested.
text_raw: May these hands be pure and disinterested.

text: Remember that you are the guardians of beauty in the world.
text_raw: Remember that you are the guardians of beauty in the world.

text: May that suffice to free you from tastes which are passing and have no genuine value, to free you from the search after strange or unbecoming expressions.
text_raw:
May that suffice to free you from tastes which are passing and 
have no genuine value, to free you from the search after 
strange or unbecoming expressions.

text: Be always and everywhere worthy of your ideals and you will be worthy of the Church which, by our voice, addresses to you today her message of friendship, salvation, grace, and benediction.
text_raw:
Be always and everywhere 
worthy of your ideals and you will be worthy of the Church

proud to have glorified and liberated woman, and in the

text: That is why, at this moment when the human race is undergoing so deep a transformation, women impregnated with the spirit of the gospel can do much to aid mankind in not falling.
text_raw:
That is why, at this moment when 
the human race is undergoing so deep a transformation, 
women impregnated with the spirit of the gospel can do

text_raw:

text: You are present in the mystery of a life beginning.

text: You offer consolation in the departure of death.

text: Our tech¬ nology runs the risk of becoming inhuman.
text_raw:
Our tech¬

text_raw:
Reconcile men 
with life and above all, we beseech you, watch carefully over

text: Hold back the hand of man who, in a moment of folly, might attempt to destroy human civilization.
text_raw:
Hold back the hand of man who, in 
a moment of folly, might attempt to destroy human

text: Wives, mothers of families, the first educators of the human race in the intimacy of the family circle, pass on to your sons and your daughters the traditions of your fathers at the same time that you prepare them for an unsearchable future.
text_raw:
Wives, mothers of families, the first educators of the 
human race in the intimacy of the family circle, pass on to 
your sons and your daughters the traditions of your fathers

text_raw:
Always remember that by her children a mother

And you, women living alone, realize what you can ac¬ 
complish through your dedicated vocation.

text: Society is appeal¬ ing to you on all sides.
text_raw:
Society is appeal¬ 
ing to you on all sides.

text_raw:
Not even families can live without the 
help of those who have no families.

text_raw:
Especially you, con¬ 
secrated virgins, in a world where egoism and the search for 
pleasure would become law, be the guardians of purity,

text: Jesus, who has given to conjugal love all its plenitudes, has also exalted the renouncement of human love when this is for the sake of divine love and for the service of all.
text_raw:
Jesus, who has given to conjugal love

text: To the Poor, the Sick, and the Suffering {Read by Paul Cardinal Meouchi, Maronite-rite Patriarch of Antioch; assisted by Stefan Cardinal Wyszynski of Warsaw and Peter Cardinal Doi of Tokyo.) To all of you, brothers in trial, who are visited by suffering under a thousand forms, the Council has a very special message.
text_raw:
To the Poor, the Sick, and the Suffering 
{Read by Paul Cardinal Meouchi, Maronite-rite Patriarch of 
Antioch; assisted by Stefan Cardinal Wyszynski of Warsaw 
and Peter Cardinal Doi of Tokyo.) 
To all of you, brothers in trial, who are visited by suffering 
under a thousand forms, the Council has a very special 
message.

text: It feels fixed on itself your pleading eyes, burning with fever or hollow with fatigue, questioning eyes which search in vain for the why of human suffering and which ask anxiously when and whence will come relief.
text_raw:
It feels fixed on itself your pleading eyes, burning 
with fever or hollow with fatigue, questioning eyes which 
search in vain for the why of human suffering and which 
ask anxiously when and whence will come relief.

text: Very dear brothers, we feel echoing deeply within our hearts as fathers and pastors your laments and your com¬ plaints.
text_raw:
Very dear brothers, we feel echoing deeply within our 
hearts as fathers and pastors your laments and your com¬ 
plaints.

text: Our suffering is increased at the thought that it is not within our power to bring you bodily help nor the lessen¬ ing of your physical sufferings, which physicians, nurses, and all those dedicated to the service of the sick are endeavoring to relieve as best they can.
text_raw:
Our suffering is increased at the thought that it is 
not within our power to bring you bodily help nor the lessen¬ 
ing of your physical sufferings, which physicians, nurses, and 
all those dedicated to the service of the sick are endeavoring 
to relieve as best they can.

text: But we have something deeper and more valuable to give you, the only truth capable of answering the mystery of suffering and of bringing you relief without illusion, and that is faith and union with the Man of Sorrows, with Christ the Son of God, nailed to the cross for our sins and for our salvation.
text_raw:
But we have something deeper and more valuable to give 
you, the only truth capable of answering the mystery of 
suffering and of bringing you relief without illusion, and that

Son of God, nailed to the cross for our sins and for our 
salvation.

text: Christ did not do away with suffering.

text: He did not even wish to unveil to us entirely the mystery of suffering.
text_raw:
He did not 
even wish to unveil to us entirely the mystery of suffering.

text_raw:
He

weight of the cross, you who are poor and abandoned, you

text: To Workers (Read by Paul Cardinal Zoungrana of Ouagadougou [Upper Volta], assisted by Jose Cardinal Quintero of Caracas and Jose Cardinal Bueno y Monreale of Seville.) In the course of this Council, we, the Catholic bishops of the five continents, have, among many other subjects, reflected together on the grave questions posed for human conscience by the economic and social conditions of the contemporary world, the coexistence of nations, the problem of armaments, of war and peace.
text_raw:
To Workers 
(Read by Paul Cardinal Zoungrana of Ouagadougou [Upper 
Volta], assisted by Jose Cardinal Quintero of Caracas and 
Jose Cardinal Bueno y Monreale of Seville.) 
In the course of this Council, we, the Catholic bishops of the 
five continents, have, among many other subjects, reflected 
together on the grave questions posed for human conscience 
by the economic and social conditions of the contemporary 
world, the coexistence of nations, the problem of armaments, 
of war and peace.

text: We are fully aware of the repercussions which the solution provided for these problems can have on the concrete life of the working men and women of the entire world.
text_raw:
We are fully aware of the repercussions 
which the solution provided for these problems can have on 
the concrete life of the working men and women of the entire 
world.

text: Thus, at the end of our deliberations, we wish to address to all of them a message of confidence, peace, and friendship.
text_raw:
Thus, at the end of our deliberations, we wish to 
address to all of them a message of confidence, peace, and 
friendship.

text: Very loved sons, rest assured first of all that the Church is aware of your sufferings, your struggles, and your hopes, and that she appreciates highly the virtues which ennoble your souls—namely, courage, dedication, professional conscience, love of justice—and that she recognizes fully the immense services which, each in his own place and in positions often the most obscure and the most ignored, you render to the whole of society.
text_raw:

aware of your sufferings, your struggles, and your hopes, and

souls—namely, courage, dedication, professional conscience,

whole of society.

text: The Church is grateful to you for this and thanks you through our voice.
text_raw:
The Church is grateful to you for this and 
thanks you through our voice.

text: In these recent years, she has never ceased to keep before her eyes the increasingly complex problems of the working world; and the echo which recent pontifical encyclicals have found in your ranks has proved to what degree the soul of the workingman of our time was attuned to that of his highest spiritual leaders.

world; and the echo which recent pontifical encyclicals have

text: She has confidence that you will find such strength and such joy that you will not be tempted, as were some of your elders, to yield to the seductions of egoistic or hedonistic philosophies or to those of despair and annihilation, and that in the face of atheism, a phenomenon of lassitude and old age, you will know how to affirm your faith in life and in what gives meaning to life, that is to say, the certitude of the existence of a just and good God.

She has confidence that you will find such 
strength and such joy that you will not be tempted, as were 
some of your elders, to yield to the seductions of egoistic or 
hedonistic philosophies or to those of despair and annihilation,

text: It is in the name of this God and of His Son, Jesus, that we exhort you to open your hearts to the dimensions of the world, to heed the appeal of your brothers, to place your youthful energies at their service.

It is in the name of this God and of His Son, Jesus, that we 
exhort you to open your hearts to the dimensions of the 
world, to heed the appeal of your brothers, to place your 
youthful energies at their service.

text: Fight against all egoism.
text_raw: Fight against all egoism.

text: Refuse to give free course to the instincts of violence and hatred which beget wars and all their train of miseries.

text: Be generous, pure, respectful, and sincere, and build in en¬ thusiasm a better world than your elders had.

generous, pure, respectful, and sincere, and build in en¬ 
thusiasm a better world than your elders had.

text: The Church looks to you with confidence and with love.

text: Rich with a long past ever living in her, and marching on toward human perfection in time and the ultimate destinies of history and of life, the Church is the real youth of the world.

world.

text: She possesses what constitutes the strength and the charm of youth, that is to say, the ability to rejoice with what is beginning, to give oneself unreservedly, to renew oneself and to set out again for new conquests.

text: Papal Brief Declaring the Council Completed At the closing ceremonies, on December 8, 1965, Archbishop Pericle Felici, General Secretary of the Council, read the papal brief declaring the Second Vatican Council closed and stating that all of its decrees should be “religiously observed by all the faithful.” Pope Paul VI: for perpetual memory of the event:
text_raw:
Papal Brief Declaring 
the Council Completed 
At the closing ceremonies, on December 8, 1965, Archbishop 
Pericle Felici, General Secretary of the Council, read the 
papal brief declaring the Second Vatican Council closed and 
stating that all of its decrees should be “religiously observed 
by all the faithful.” 
Pope Paul VI: for perpetual memory of the event:

text: Prayer of Pope John XXIII to the Holy Spirit for the Success of the Ecumenical Council O Holy Spirit, sent by the Father in the name of Jesus, who art present in the Church and dost infallibly guide it, pour forth, we pray, the fullness of Thy gifts upon the Ecumenical Council.

Prayer of Pope John XXIII 
to the Holy Spirit 
for the Success of 
the Ecumenical Council 
O Holy Spirit, sent by the Father in the name of Jesus, who 
art present in the Church and dost infallibly guide it, pour 
forth, we pray, the fullness of Thy gifts upon the Ecumenical 
Council.

text: Enlighten, O most gracious Teacher and Comforter, the minds of our prelates who, in prompt response to the Supreme Roman Pontiff, will carry on the sessions of the Sacred Council.
text_raw:
Enlighten, O most gracious Teacher and Comforter, the 
minds of our prelates who, in prompt response to the Supreme 
Roman Pontiff, will carry on the sessions of the Sacred 
Council.

text: Grant that from this Council abundant fruit may ripen; that the light and strength of the gospel may be extended more and more in human society; that the Catholic religion and its active missionary works may flourish with ever greater vigor, with the happy result that knowledge of the Church’s teaching may spread and Christian morality have a salutary increase.
text_raw:
Grant that from this Council abundant fruit may ripen; 
that the light and strength of the gospel may be extended 
more and more in human society; that the Catholic religion 
and its active missionary works may flourish with ever greater 
vigor, with the happy result that knowledge of the Church’s 
teaching may spread and Christian morality have a salutary 
increase.

text: O sweet Guest of the soul, strengthen our minds in the truth and dispose our hearts to pay reverential heed, that we may accept with sincere submission those things which shall be decided in the Council and fulfill them with ready will.
text_raw:
O sweet Guest of the soul, strengthen our minds in the 
truth and dispose our hearts to pay reverential heed, that 
we may accept with sincere submission those things which 
shall be decided in the Council and fulfill them with ready 
will.

text: We pray also for those sheep who are not now of the one fold of Jesus Christ, that even as they glory in the name of Christian, they may come at last to unity under the governance of the one Shepherd.
text_raw:
We pray also for those sheep who are not now of the 
one fold of Jesus Christ, that even as they glory in the name 
of Christian, they may come at last to unity under the 
governance of the one Shepherd.

text: Renew Thy wonders in this our day, as by a new Pentecost.

text: Grant to Thy Church that, being of one mind and steadfast in prayer with Mary, the Mother of Jesus, and following the lead of blessed Peter, it may advance the reign of our Divine Savior, the reign of truth and justice, the reign of love and peace.

in prayer with Mary, the Mother of Jesus, and following the 
lead of blessed Peter, it may advance the reign of our Divine

peace.
